title: Sort Matrix by Diagonals
summary: Given an n x n matrix of integers, sort the matrix so that the bottom-left diagonals are in non-increasing order and the top-right diagonals are in non-decreasing order.
statement: Given an n x n matrix of integers, sort the matrix so that the bottom-left diagonals are in non-increasing order and the top-right diagonals are in non-decreasing order.
constraints: grid is a nonempty n by n integer matrix with n <= 10.
Diagonals beginning in the first column, including the main diagonal, must be non-increasing from top-left to bottom-right.
Diagonals beginning in the top row to the right of the main diagonal must be non-decreasing in that direction.
reference_solution:
def sort_matrix_diagonals(grid):
    n=len(grid)
    for start_row in range(n):
        values=[];row=start_row;column=0
        while row<n and column<n:values.append(grid[row][column]);row+=1;column+=1
        values.sort();row=start_row;column=0
        while row<n and column<n:grid[row][column]=values.pop();row+=1;column+=1
    for start_column in range(1,n):
        values=[];row=0;column=start_column
        while row<n and column<n:values.append(grid[row][column]);row+=1;column+=1
        values.sort(reverse=True);row=0;column=start_column
        while row<n and column<n:grid[row][column]=values.pop();row+=1;column+=1
    return grid

hints: Every cell belongs to exactly one diagonal identified by row minus column.
Process first-column starts and top-row starts separately because their required order differs.
Collect a diagonal, sort it, and write it back in traversal order with descending values below-left and ascending values above-right.
Independent diagonal sorting cannot interfere because diagonals partition the matrix.

tests.explanation: The main and lower diagonals descend while upper diagonals ascend, producing [[8,2,3],[9,6,7],[4,5,1]].
Sorting the main diagonal downward gives [[3,1],[4,2]].
